title: Towards a user-centric HPC-QC environment
problem: Hybrid HPC-QPU systems lack robust execution environment for hybrid quantum-classical programs; integration challenges in scheduling, portability, and reproducibility.
method: HPC-QC middleware with second-layer scheduling post-HPC manager for QPU utilization; vendor-neutral QRMI support; monitoring and observability stack.

title: MLPerf Power: Benchmarking the Energy Efficiency of Machine Learning Systems from μWatts to MWatts for Sustainable AI
problem: There is no standardized, cross-platform methodology for benchmarking the energy efficiency of ML systems spanning the full deployment range from sub-milliwatt IoT devices to megawatt-scale datacenter clusters. Existing benchmarks focus on throughput/latency without capturing power consumption in a reproducible, comparable way across heterogeneous hardware.
method: MLPerf Power extends the MLPerf benchmark suite with standardized power measurement rules and best practices developed by a consortium of 20+ industry organizations. The methodology defines measurement protocols for power metering at different granularities (device, rack, facility) and applies them to representative ML workloads (inference and training) across edge, mobile, and datacenter deployment scales. 1,841 reproducible measurements were collected from 60 systems, enabling cross-architecture energy-efficiency comparisons.

title: Precon: A Precision-Convertible Architecture for Accelerating Quantized Deep Learning Models across Various Domains Including LLMs
problem: LLMs are highly sensitive to quantization precision; existing accelerators are tailored to specific low-precision schemes (weight-only, mixed-precision), creating inefficiencies when switching between INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT8 arithmetic across different models.
method: Precon enables on-the-fly precision switching via a precision-convertible processing unit. Shared logic supports half-float (FP16) decoding and integer (INT) decomposition, allowing the same hardware to execute INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT4-INT8 arithmetic by controlling datapath routing and operation sequencing.

title: 22.5 A 0.3pJ/b 32Gb/s/Pin Single-Ended PAM-4 Receiver with a Delay-Less Capacitive-Feedback Equalizer
problem: Multi-level signaling (PAM4) increases data throughput for memory and I/O interfaces but reduces SNR, requiring complex equalization that increases power consumption and area. Traditional equalization circuits introduce delay and complexity.
method: A delay-less capacitive-feedback equalizer (CFE) performs PAM4 signal equalization without introducing pipeline delay. The receiver is implemented in 28nm CMOS, enabling a simple, power-efficient equalization structure that directly compensates for channel ISI.

title: 18.3: A 93.3dB SNDR, 180.4dB FoMs Calibration-Free Noise-Shaping Pipelined-SAR ADC with Cross-Stage Gain-Mismatch-Error-Shaping Technique and Negative-R-Assisted Residue Integrator
problem: High-resolution pipelined-SAR ADCs suffer from mismatch errors and inter-stage gain errors; prior gain-error-shaping (GES) schemes introduce multi-bit feedback with additional mismatch sources (truncation and quantization noise) requiring extensive calibration.
method: A calibration-free pipelined-SAR ADC uses cross-stage gain-mismatch-error-shaping that directly combines GES and MES without multi-bit feedback, leveraging a negative-resistance-assisted residue integrator to enable efficient analog integration and error shaping.

title: Expanding Logical Space Freely: A Memory-efficient Mapping Table Design for Compressional SSDs
problem: Reducing memory footprint of Logical-to-Physical (L2P) address mapping tables in compressional SSDs, which compress logical pages to improve capacity but increase mapping table size and pressure on in-SSD memory.
method: N-to-1 L2P mapping table design consolidates multiple logical entries into single entries, eliminating duplication of physical page numbers when a physical page contains multiple compressed logical pages. Promotion/demotion mechanisms enable entries to migrate across pages with different compression ratios; compression-aware garbage collection algorithm minimizes copy operations for partially invalid physical pages due to N-to-1 mapping.

title: GPart: A GNN-Enabled Multilevel Graph Partitioner
problem: Large-scale graph partitioning requires balancing cut minimization and memory efficiency; existing multilevel methods like METIS use heuristic coarsening and refinement, missing learning-based optimization.
method: A scalable multilevel framework integrating GNN embeddings with traditional coarsening and refinement techniques. GNN embeddings capture graph structure for improved partitioning decisions during multilevel optimization. Efficient hierarchical coarsening reduces problem size while GNN guidance refines partition quality.

title: NSFlow: An End-to-End FPGA Framework with Scalable Dataflow Architecture for Neuro-Symbolic AI
problem: Neuro-Symbolic AI workloads exhibit heterogeneous kernels and unique memory access patterns unsuitable for general-purpose ML accelerators (CPU/GPU/TPU).
method: NSFlow features a design architecture generator identifying data dependencies and creating optimized dataflows, plus a reconfigurable FPGA array with flexible compute units, reorganizable memory, and mixed-precision capabilities.

title: Cuzco: A High-Performance RISC-V RVA23 Compatible CPU IP
problem: RISC-V ecosystem lacks high-performance, production-grade CPU implementations; Cuzco provides a high-performance RISC-V core compatible with RVA23 profile for data center and edge deployment.
method: Cuzco implements a high-performance RISC-V core with multi-stage pipelined execution, out-of-order instruction scheduling, and caches optimized for latency-sensitive workloads, full compliance with RVA23 ISA specification.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper Demystifying the Resilience of Large Language Model Inference: An End-to-End Perspective
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility verification of LLM inference resilience research.
method: Artifact evaluation following SC25 reproducibility guidelines; independent testing of LLM inference resilience experiments.

title: A Practical Quantum Solver for Multidimensional Partial Differential Equations
problem: Solving multidimensional PDEs with low accuracy and high execution time on quantum devices
method: Two algorithm variants: (1) FDM+C2Q+numerical instantiation, (2) FDM+C2Q+column-by-column decomposition for enhanced accuracy and scalability

title: Process Only Where You Look: Hardware and Algorithm Co-optimization for Efficient Gaze-Tracked Foveated Rendering in Virtual Reality
problem: Image rendering in VR head-mounted displays (HMDs) is computationally expensive, particularly for real-time applications where low latency is mandatory. Existing gaze-tracking and foveated rendering approaches impose high algorithmic and hardware costs that compound the overall rendering budget.
method: The paper proposes POLONet, an efficient multitask deep learning framework for real-time eye-movement tracking, co-designed with a dedicated POLO accelerator integrated as a plug-in for VR HMD SoCs. The system exploits the observation that human gaze is concentrated in a small foveal region, so full-resolution rendering is performed only where the eye is looking while peripheral regions are rendered at reduced quality. The hardware-algorithm co-optimization jointly minimizes gaze-tracking latency and rendering compute cost through a tightly coupled accelerator-SoC interface.

title: COGENT: Adaptable Compiler Toolchain for Tagging RISC-V Binaries
problem: Adding hardware-enforced metadata tags to RISC-V binaries for security and testing policies currently requires tedious, architecture-specific compiler modifications; there is no flexible, reusable toolchain that can emit variable-width tags at multiple granularities (instruction, basic block, function) from a single compilation pipeline.
method: COGENT is an LLVM-based compiler toolchain for RISC-V that generates instruction-level metadata tags. It supports variable-width tags (1–32 bits per instruction) and arbitrary-width tags per function or basic block, at selectable granularities. The toolchain includes a tag-aware disassembler and a tag integrity checker. A control-flow label emission pass marks branch targets and call sites, enabling CFI enforcement downstream. The pipeline is extensible to new tag policies without modifying the core compiler.

title: Empowering Vector Architectures for ML: The CAMP Architecture for Matrix Multiplication
problem: Existing vector architectures (VAs) and SIMD units—including ARM SVE and RISC-V SIMD—cannot efficiently execute quantized neural network (QNN) matrix multiplication at 4-bit and 8-bit integer precisions because their datapaths are designed for wider, fixed-width computations.
method: CAMP (Cartesian Accumulative Matrix Pipeline) introduces a hybrid multiplier that hierarchically decomposes quantized integer multiplication into a two-level Cartesian product structure. The architecture natively handles multiple integer precisions (focus on INT4 and INT8) within the same datapath by exploiting structural regularity of quantized GEMM. CAMP is integrated as a micro-architecture extension to ARM A64FX (ARMv8 SVE, synthesized at TSMC 7 nm with Synopsys ICC2) and a RISC-V edge SoC (GlobalFoundries 22 nm, Cadence Innovus), adding 1% and 4% area overhead respectively.

title: 22.2: An 850µW 2-to-5GHz Jitter-Filtering and Instant-Toggling Injection-Locked Quadrature-Clock Generator for Low-Power Clock Distribution in HBM Interfaces
problem: HBM (high-bandwidth memory) interfaces require parallel distribution of four quadrature clocks across multiple data groups, consuming significant power, introducing quadrature error, and suffering power-supply-induced jitter during long routings.
method: Injection-locked quadrature-clock generator operating at 2-5GHz with jitter filtering and instant-toggling capability, distributed across DQ groups to locally generate quadrature clocks from differential WDQS reference.

title: 17.3 A 30.4GOPS/mW MK-CKKS Processor for Secure Multi-Party Computation
problem: Multi-key fully homomorphic encryption (MK-FHE) processors for secure multi-party computation face challenges in integrating flexible configuration of task-, ciphertext-, and polynomial-level operations into a single area-efficient hardware architecture that scales to an unlimited number of parties.
method: The processor implements a flexible, scalable architecture for MK-CKKS that supports variable task-level configurations (linear/nonlinear transformations) composed from ciphertext-level operations (multiplication, key-switching, rescaling) and polynomial-level operations (NTT, base conversion, permutations) optimized for area efficiency.
